request.system:
Explain the result of an optimization model to someone who isn't an expert, in 3 to 5 sentences: what to do, what it achieves, and what limits it.

Use only the facts you're given: the decision values, the objective value, which constraints are binding (fully used), the slack in the others, and shadow prices if given (how much the objective changes per extra unit of a constraint's limit). Don't compute new numbers. Every number you write must appear in the facts, the model, or the problem, at most rounded.

content.text: The bakery should make 20 chocolate cakes and 30 vanilla cakes each day. Together these bring in a profit of $530. Vanilla cakes are the more profitable of the two, so they are made up to the 30 that customers will buy, and the rest of the daily capacity goes to chocolate. The limit is the 50-cake daily production capacity, which is completely used, and the vanilla demand of 30, which is also fully used. Chocolate demand is not the constraint, since 30 chocolate cakes of demand go unmet, but the staffing limit means the bakery can't make more.
